newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX bullish at start, but EMU angst remains.
newsitem.headline: German DAX bullish at start, but EMU angst remains.

text.p: German shares took their cue from Wall Street and the dollar early on Thursday to post solid gains on healthy volumes, but dealers said ongoing uncertainty about monetary union would likely cap market gains.
"We are delighted to see the market getting back in step with Wall Street," said one dealer.
"But if we don't get a clear message from (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel and (Bundesbank President Hans) Tietmeyer today, this will still be a nervous market."
The Bundesbank is expected to discuss Waigel's plans to revalue assets at its regular council meeting today.

The plans triggered an unprecedented dispute between Bonn and the central bank, which viewed an original proposal to use the revaluation proceeds to help German meet Maastricht deficit goals as unacceptable.
It remains unclear whether the Bundesbank will issue a statement on the issue today.
Share prices were also being influenced by next week's expiry of DAX otions contracts on the DTB exchange, which always causes fluctuations on the cash market.
Dealers said the most actively traded option aimed for a strike price of 3,700 DAX points.
At 0753 GMT, the IBIS DAX index was up 28.33 points at 3,700.20 points.
June DTB DAX futures were up 23 points at 3,702 points.

The gains were sparked by the Dow Jones' ascent to its fourth consecutive record close while the dollar firmed to trade at 1.725 against the mark -- always a good signal for Germany's dollar-sensitive exporters.
"All in all we have a strong operating environment and the dollar is adding some extra pep," said a Munich trader.
The Bundesbank was universally expected to keep interest rates on hold after its meeting.
All 30 blue chip stocks were showing a mild advance in early trade.

The chief underperformer was chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Altana AG after it issued a statement late on Wednesday countering market rumours that it was either to be taken over or planned to launch a new drug in the U.S. soon.
Altana said it expected approval to start testing a respiratory drug in the near future but that the drug could not be launched for several years.
"That was disappointing," said one trader. "Tests alone mean nothing. It (the drug) might never hit the market."
The company also said there was no truth in rumours of a takeover.
Altana shares were down 30 marks, or 1.7 percent, at 1,750 marks, but were off a low of 1,715 marks.
